boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all five frozen records in the Confederate Heartland Offensive. Preserve per-engagement dates; the live NPS campaign heading (June-October 1862) does not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: NPS says Mitchel ordered an expedition to capture Chattanooga; Cist describes an expedition against the town that bombarded it and made a demonstration of crossing.
claims.rationale: Stated mission versus executed action; no original order was inspected. Whether the demonstration reflected a changed objective is not established.

claims.value: Mitchel ordered the expedition and Negley commanded it. On the Confederate side, NPS says the listed commander, Kirby Smith, arrived on the 8th, and Cist quotes Duke naming Leadbetter as commandant of the place.
claims.rationale: The frozen principal Confederate commander arrived during the two-day interval; local command and departmental authority are different roles, and neither receives automatic sole credit. Live heading ranks (Major General Negley; Lieutenant General Smith) conflict with the frozen ranks and are not adopted.

open_questions: Original orders, returns, casualty reconciliation, Confederate knowledge of the approach and the effective local command clock remain deferred after the bounded pass. The June 7–8 interval excludes the earlier Jasper action.
NPS/CWSAC is one family; Cist is one interested retrospective Union staff history. Quoted reports and participant accounts inside Cist are not additional independently inspected families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
